items.title: Material Receipt Note (GRN)
items.context: Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection > Material Receipt Note (GRN)

cards.title: What does a Material Receipt Note record?
cards.body:
A **Material Receipt Note** records goods that physically arrived at a warehouse from a vendor or another unit.
- It separates **accepted**, **rejected**, **free** and replaceable quantities.
**Watch out:** stock only rises once the receipt is **authorized**.

cards.title: What can a receipt be raised against?
cards.body:
A receipt is raised against a **Purchase Order**, a **Gate Entry**, a **Stock Transfer**, or **directly** with no reference.
- The source decides which fields can still be edited.
**Watch out:** some companies require raw material to arrive through a **Gate Entry**.

cards.title: How are accepted quantity and the line amount worked out on a receipt?
cards.body:
The receipt calculates **accepted quantity** and amount, so the storekeeper enters only what was counted.
**How it works:**
- **Accepted** = received minus rejected minus free-of-cost quantity (material sent without charge).
- **Amount** = accepted quantity times rate.
- For Purchase Order and Gate Entry receipts, accepted plus rejected plus free must equal the received quantity.
**Why it matters:** every unit counted at the gate is accounted for, and only accepted units are valued.
**Example:** received 300, free 20, rejected 0, rate ₹40: accepted is 280, amount ₹11,200.
**Watch out:** companies that validate on challan quantity compare against the challan, not the received quantity.

cards.title: Why did stock not rise when stores saved the receipt?
cards.body:
A saved receipt does not always add stock. Stock rises only when the receipt reaches **Authorized**.
**How it works:**
- **Initial** and **Release** save the receipt, and Release records who released it.
- **Authorized** records the authorizer and date, and posts the accepted quantity to stock.
- The stock month must not be locked by month-end closing.
**Why it matters:** a receipt is checked before the company counts the material as usable.
**Watch out:** when inspection is required, the receipt is flagged as waiting for inspection until it is done.

cards.title: Who can set a receipt to Authorized when multi-level approval is on?
cards.body:
With **multi-level approval**, a receipt cannot simply be set to Authorized by whoever saves it.
**How it works:**
- Each approver approves at their own level in the approval panel.
- Only the **last-level approver** can authorize, after approving there.
- For that approver the screen switches the status from Release to Authorized.
**Why it matters:** the final approval, and the stock posting that follows it, rests with one accountable level.
**Watch out:** choosing Authorized earlier gives the message that the last level has not approved.

cards.title: Order of 1,000 with 3 percent tolerance: what happens when 1,040 arrive?
cards.body:
A receipt compares the quantity arriving, plus what was already received, with the **order quantity plus tolerance**. Tolerance is either a fixed quantity or a percentage.
**Rule:**
- The screen warns when received quantity goes above the order plus tolerance. A company can set this check to block instead of warn.
- A further check refuses accepted quantity above the open balance plus tolerance.
**What it affects:** a refused receipt is not saved, so stock and the supplier's bill do not move.
**Worked example:**
- Order 1,000 units, tolerance 3 percent, nothing received yet, so the limit is 1,030.
- 1,040 arrive: the screen warns, because 1,040 is above 1,030.
- If the user continues, the accepted quantity of 1,040 is still refused. Accepting 1,030 passes.
**If it goes wrong:** the extra 10 units cannot go on this receipt. Ask Purchase to amend the order before receiving more.

cards.title: What happens to other records when an authorized receipt is deleted?
cards.body:
An **authorized** receipt can still be deleted, but only while none of its stock has been used. There is no cancelled status.
**Rule:**
- Delete asks for confirmation. It is refused if stock from the receipt has been issued, if a tyre repair entry exists, or if the stock month is locked.
**What it affects:**
- The stock lots, the finance voucher and the other records created by the receipt are removed.
- The statuses of the order, gate entry and request it was received against are restored.
**Worked example:** a receipt for 100 bearings was authorized to the wrong warehouse. Nothing is issued, so it is deleted: the 100 leave stock and the order shows 100 open again. Had 10 been issued first, delete would be refused with the issue number.
**If it goes wrong:** once stock is used the receipt cannot be deleted, and an authorized receipt cannot be saved again, so escalate to your supervisor.

cards.title: What does a Purchase Order commit the company to?
cards.body:
A **Purchase Order** is a commitment to a vendor for items or services at agreed rates, quantities, delivery dates and terms.
- It should be raised only against valid demand, approved rates and available budget.
**Watch out:** the right people must **authorize** it before goods are received.

cards.title: What can a Purchase Order be raised from?
cards.body:
A Purchase Order can be raised from an approved **Purchase Request**, a **vendor quotation**, an **agreement**, or directly by the buyer.
- A **drop-shipment** order is raised against a customer's sales order.
**Watch out:** the order quantity cannot exceed what is still open on its source.

cards.title: How is a Purchase Order authorized when approval has several levels?
cards.body:
Under **multi-level approval** the status of an order cannot be set to Authorized directly.
**How it works:**
- The order moves to **Release**, and the first approval level becomes ready.
- The **authorization group** is chosen from the order's net amount, and chosen again whenever the net amount changes.
- Approvers approve or reject level by level in the approval panel.
- A user with amount limits can authorize only within those limits.
**Why it matters:** bigger orders reach the approvers set for their value.
**Watch out:** once released, only users assigned to the group can update the order.

cards.title: A buyer orders 350 units against a request with 300 still open: what happens?
cards.body:
An order line cannot ask for more than what is **still open** on the document it came from.
**Rule:**
- The order quantity is checked against the open balance of the purchase request, the comparative statement booking, or the agreement quantity, amount or schedule.
- A line above that balance is refused when the order is saved.
**What it affects:** the demand stays tied to the approvals and budget of its source, so buying cannot silently grow.
**Worked example:**
- A purchase request asked for 500 units and 200 are already on earlier orders, so 300 are open.
- The buyer enters 350: the save is refused with a message that the order quantity exceeds the balance.
**If it goes wrong:** order 300, or ask the requester for a further purchase request for the extra 50.

cards.title: What is a Purchase Request for?
cards.body:
A **Purchase Request** is a department's priced, approved statement of what it needs to buy, how much, by when and for which cost center.
- The purchase team later turns it into **purchase orders**.
**Watch out:** buying should start only from an approved, **budget-checked** request.

cards.title: What changes on a Purchase Request raised from a Material Request?
cards.body:
A Purchase Request can start from a **Material Request** that the store could not meet.
**How it works:**
- Request type, department and requested-by are copied and **locked**.
- Quantity defaults to the outstanding balance, and rate to the last purchase rate in the line unit.
- Items not in the chosen warehouse are left out.
- Saving a line updates that line's status on the Material Request.
**Why it matters:** the Material Request always shows how much has been taken forward.
**Watch out:** the required quantity is locked on the Purchase Request.

cards.title: A request is above the department budget: is it blocked, and what is checked?
cards.body:
A Purchase Request is checked against the **authorised budgets** valid on its document date.
**Rule:**
- Four budgets are checked: the division total, the department total, each item line, and each cost center.
- An overrun shows the remaining amount.
- It blocks the save only when the company's budget validation setting is on.
**What it affects:** a blocked request is not saved, so it cannot be turned into an order.
**Worked example:**
- The department has 40,000 left in its budget and the request totals 55,000.
- The message shows the 40,000 remaining.
- With the setting on, the request cannot be saved. With it off, the request saves and the overrun is only a message.
**If it goes wrong:** cut the quantities to fit, or ask for the budget to be revised before saving again.

items.title: Gate Entry
items.context: Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection > Gate Entry

cards.title: What is a Gate Entry, and when is it made?
cards.body:
A **Gate Entry** is the first record of an inward vehicle and its material, made at the gate before the receipt.
- It notes the supplier, the reference documents and the quantities on the supplier's **challan** (delivery note).
**Watch out:** it records arrival and does not add stock.

cards.title: Why can a gate entry be used for only one receipt?
cards.body:
A **Gate Entry** can be linked to only one **receipt**.
**How it works:**
- A receipt that picks a gate entry already used on another receipt is refused.
- The receipt updates the gate entry's received quantity, unless weighment controls it.
- A gate entry cannot be deleted once a receipt, a weighment slip or a vehicle gate-out exists against it.
**Why it matters:** one arrival is matched to one receipt, so the same delivery cannot be received twice.
**Watch out:** to remove a gate entry, first deal with the documents that depend on it.

cards.title: How does a Gate Entry stop over-supply against an order?
cards.body:
The gate entry refuses a **challan quantity** above the order's open balance plus tolerance.
**How it works:**
- Tolerance is either a quantity or a percentage of the order quantity.
- It is checked when the quantity is typed and again when the entry is saved.
- The check is skipped for orders that are manually closing.
**Example:** open balance 400, order 1,000, tolerance 5 percent: the most that can be entered is 450.
**Watch out:** over-supply is stopped at the gate, before the receipt is made.

cards.title: What is a Purchase Order Amendment for?
cards.body:
A **Purchase Order Amendment** is a controlled, numbered change to an already authorized order, such as a new rate, quantity or delivery date.
- Each version keeps its own number, date, reason and status.
**Watch out:** the live order follows the last **authorized** amendment.

cards.title: Which orders can be amended, and what stays fixed?
cards.body:
Only an order whose latest version is **authorized** can be amended.
**How it works:**
- The order list offers orders that are Authorized or In Progress, or Completed with an authorized change of status.
- Vendor, location, order type, purchase type and category, reference and order date are copied from the order and cannot be changed.
- A **reason** for the amendment is mandatory.
**Why it matters:** the history of the order is kept version by version.
**Watch out:** a cancelled order, or a completed order that was not re-opened, cannot be amended.

cards.title: An order line of 500 has 300 received: can an amendment cut it to 250?
cards.body:
An amendment cannot undo what has already been **received** against the order.
**Rule:**
- A line with received quantity cannot be unselected or deleted, and its make and technical grade cannot change.
- Its quantity cannot go below the quantity already received.
- Order quantity cannot exceed the quantity of the purchase request it came from.
**What it affects:** when the amendment is authorized, the live order is replaced by the amendment, and the request quantities are reversed and applied again.
**Worked example:**
- An order line of 500 units has 300 received.
- An amendment to 250 is refused, because 250 is below the 300 received. An amendment to 400 is allowed, if the request has room for it.
**If it goes wrong:** to stop further deliveries, change the quantity to what is already received, here 300.

items.title: Inspection Intimation
items.context: Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection > Inspection Intimation

cards.title: What does an Inspection Intimation do?
cards.body:
An **Inspection Intimation** is a numbered letter that tells the inspecting department which received items are waiting for inspection.
- It is raised after the receipt is made and before the receipt is authorized.
**Watch out:** it requests inspection; the **Inspection Entry** records the result.

cards.title: Which receipt lines can be put on an Inspection Intimation?
cards.body:
An **Inspection Intimation** lists only the receipt lines that are ready to be sent for inspection.
**How it works:**
- The receipt must be flagged as requiring inspection and must not yet be authorized.
- It must be in the same division and within the date range chosen.
- Each selected line needs a department, and a line can be on only one intimation.
**Why it matters:** each line is sent for inspection once, to the right department.
**Watch out:** the receipt date cannot be later than the intimation date.

items.title: Inspection Entry
items.context: Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection > Inspection Entry

cards.title: What does an Inspection Entry record?
cards.body:
An **Inspection Entry** records the result of quality inspection on received goods: accepted and rejected quantity, the reason, and quality readings.
- Only accepted material is taken into stock; rejections are documented for **vendor follow-up**.
**Watch out:** it is made after the **Inspection Intimation** is authorized.

cards.title: What must be in place before an inspection result can be recorded?
cards.body:
An **Inspection Entry** can only record the result for lines that are ready for it.
**How it works:**
- The line must be on an **authorized** Inspection Intimation.
- Its receipt must not yet be authorized, and the line must not be on another inspection entry.
- The Inspection Officer cannot be blank, and a reason is mandatory when anything is rejected.
**Why it matters:** inspection happens before the receipt is authorized and stock is posted, and each line is judged once.
**Watch out:** accepted quantity cannot exceed the quantity received.

cards.title: 100 units were received and 10 fail inspection: what changes on the receipt?
cards.body:
When an **Inspection Entry** is authorized, its result is written back to the receipt, so only accepted material reaches stock.
**Rule:**
- Rejected quantity is set on the receipt line, and the accepted quantity and the stock quantity are reduced by it.
- Where the line had a single reserve row, the reserved quantity is reduced as well.
**What it affects:** the receipt can then be authorized with the corrected quantities.
**Worked example:**
- 100 units are received and the inspection rejects 10.
- The receipt line shows 90 accepted and 10 rejected. Stock is posted for 90.
**If it goes wrong:** the entry cannot be deleted once any receipt on it is authorized, so check the result before authorizing.

cards.title: Why is an authorized document locked, and how is it changed?
cards.body:
Most transaction documents are **locked** once authorized, because stock, bills and other documents start to depend on them.
**How it works:**
- Purchase Orders, Purchase Requests, Gate Entries, receipts and inspection records all refuse a second save once authorized.
- A Purchase Order is changed through an **amendment**, which is approved before it takes effect.
- A receipt cannot be saved again, but can be deleted while none of its stock is used.
**Why it matters:** a silent edit would break the link between the document and what is built on it.
**Watch out:** locked does not mean final, and each document has its own delete rules.

cards.title: What do Initial, Release and Authorized mean on a document?
cards.body:
Documents move through **Initial**, **Release** and **Authorized**.
- **Initial** is a saved draft.
- **Release** hands it on and records who and when.
- **Authorized** records the approver and locks it.
**Watch out:** under multi-level approval, Release readies the first approval level.

cards.title: Why can a document under multi-level approval not be set to Authorized directly?
cards.body:
With **multi-level approval** a document can reach Authorized only through its approval levels.
**How it works:**
- Purchase Requests, Purchase Orders, amendments and receipts all refuse a direct Authorized when the last level has not approved.
- Release makes the first level ready, and approvers are notified level by level.
- The **last-level approver** gives the final approval.
**Why it matters:** the approvals set for the document's value cannot be skipped.
**Watch out:** the approval panel only appears where multi-level approval is set up for that screen.

cards.title: When can a transaction document be deleted, and what does the delete undo?
cards.body:
A document can usually be deleted only while nothing later depends on it, and delete **undoes** its links.
**How it works:**
- A Gate Entry cannot be deleted once a receipt exists against it.
- A Material Request cannot be deleted once a purchase request or an issue was made from it.
- An inspection record cannot be deleted while a receipt on it is authorized.
- A Purchase Order cannot be deleted once an amendment or a linked advance request exists.
**Why it matters:** delete restores stock and statuses, so it must not break later documents.
**Watch out:** each form has its own rules, and a Purchase Request has no such check.

cards.title: What happens if one part of a document fails to save?
cards.body:
A document is saved **all or nothing**: the header and all its lines are saved together.
- If any part fails, nothing is saved.
**Watch out:** if someone else changed the document after you opened it, the save is refused and you must **reload**.

cards.title: What is the difference between a Gate Entry and a Material Receipt Note?
cards.body:
A **Gate Entry** records that a vehicle and its goods arrived. A **Material Receipt Note** records what was actually received and accepted.
- The gate entry comes first and limits quantities against the order.
- Only the authorized receipt adds **stock**.

cards.title: What is tolerance, and which documents check it?
cards.body:
**Tolerance** is the extra quantity allowed over an order, fixed or as a percentage.
- The order sets it for each line.
- The Gate Entry and the receipt check quantities against **balance plus tolerance**.
**Watch out:** a receipt warns first, then a final check refuses.

cards.title: Where are budgets checked in procurement, and does an overrun always stop the document?
cards.body:
Budgets are checked on the **Purchase Request**, the **Purchase Order** and the Purchase Order Amendment.
**How it works:**
- Division, department, item and cost center budgets are compared with the document value.
- On a request or order, an overrun shows the remaining amount and **blocks** only if the company's budget validation is on.
- On an amendment, the final check decides whether an overrun is a warning or a stop.
**Why it matters:** an overrun is not always a stop, so read the message.
**Watch out:** a blocked document is not saved.

cards.title: What is the order of documents from a department's need to receiving the goods?
cards.body:
Procurement moves through documents in a fixed order, and each hands over to the next.
**How it works:**
- A **Material Request** asks the store for material. What the store cannot meet becomes a **Purchase Request**.
- The buyer sends requests for quotation, records vendor quotations and compares them.
- A **Purchase Order** goes to the chosen vendor.
- At the gate a **Gate Entry** records the arrival, then the **Material Receipt Note** records the goods received.
**Why it matters:** each step is limited by the one before it, so demand, order and receipt stay linked.
**Watch out:** inspection and the purchase bill follow the receipt.

cards.title: How does each step in procurement limit the quantity of the next step?
cards.body:
Quantity is controlled at every hand-off, so more cannot be bought or received than was approved.
**How it works:**
- A **Purchase Request** raised from a material plan cannot ask for more than the plan.
- A **Purchase Order** line cannot exceed the open balance of its request or agreement.
- A **Gate Entry** challan quantity cannot exceed order balance plus tolerance.
- A **receipt** warns above balance plus tolerance and refuses accepted quantity above it.
**Why it matters:** each document stays inside the approval of the one before it.
**Watch out:** tolerance is the only room allowed above the order.

cards.title: How is a Purchase Request different from a Material Request?
cards.body:
A **Material Request** asks the store to supply material the company already stocks.
- A **Purchase Request** asks the purchase team to buy what the store cannot supply.
**Watch out:** the Purchase Request carries a price and goes through budget checks.

items.title: Goods Receipt & Quality Inspection
items.context: Goods Receipt and Quality Inspection > Whole flow

cards.title: A receipt needs inspection: in what order do the documents happen, and when does stock rise?
cards.body:
When a receipt is flagged for inspection, stock rises only after the inspection result is written back and the receipt is authorized.
**Rule:**
- The Gate Entry and the receipt are made first. The receipt is flagged as requiring inspection and is not yet authorized.
- An Inspection Intimation lists the receipt lines for inspection and is authorized.
- An Inspection Entry records accepted and rejected quantity for those lines.
- Authorizing the entry writes the rejected quantity back to the receipt, and then the receipt is authorized to post stock.
**What it affects:** rejected material never reaches stock, and the rejection is documented with a reason for vendor follow-up.
**Worked example:** 100 pumps arrive and the inspection rejects 10 for a cracked casing. The receipt then shows 90 accepted, and 90 are posted to stock.
**If it goes wrong:** a receipt cannot be deleted while its stock is used, and an inspection entry cannot be deleted once a receipt on it is authorized.
